svg.aria-label: By-reference outputs: a compiled kernel's slot buffer holds reference pairs for string, bytes, JSON, extension, and handle values; each pair names the producing step's own scratch entry, an interned constant, or an extern's stored value, and stands until an input in the step's provenance is written; every read copies out
svg.text: By-reference outputs: where a compiled kernel keeps a value that is not a number
A compiled kernel's buffer is an array of 64-bit slots. A value that does not fit a slot is kept in storage with one owner, and two slots hold a (ptr, len) pair to it.
THE SLOT BUFFER, ONE STATE'S OUTPUT IMAGE
id: u64
Imm1 · the bits themselves
Imm2 · two slots of bits
v: vec_f32
Ref2 · (ptr, len) of the elements
key: str
Ref2 · (ptr, len) of the bytes
doc: json
Ref2 · (&Value, 1)
Three colors, static and total (S1). A pair is loaded, stored, and passed by generated code; only a closure or the boundary decode dereferences it, once (S7).
Raw readers refuse a Ref2 slot (S2); the typed readers copy the value out, so what a host holds is its own.
WHO OWNS WHAT A PAIR NAMES · decided at build
The producing step's scratch entry (S3)
one per Ref2 output port, held by the state; rewritten in
place and republished when the step runs
a Ref2 extern's pair points into the value the state
stores for it, rewritten at every set_input
a string literal folded at build: the step publishes a
pair into bytes that never move and are never freed

text.tspan: A boundary value, for one call

svg.text: a cone's Ref2 input is borrowed from the interpreter's
Value for the call; its outputs are copied out first
HOW LONG THE PAIR IS VALID
key := "{region}/{id}"
prov {cycle, scale, region} · owns one Str entry
From the run that wrote it until the step's next run (S4),
and the step runs again only when an input in its
provenance is written (R1). That is the same lifetime
every other output has. Nothing reclaims the bytes on
any schedule of its own: no round, no generation, no
thread boundary. A copy step copies into its own entry.
THE INTERPRETER HOLDS VALUES; EVERY ENGINE HANDS OUT COPIES
On the interpreter every buffer entry is an owned Value (an Arc<str>, an Arc<serde_json::Value>, …), cached under the same rule. A native cone inside the
interpreter borrows its Ref2 inputs for the call and copies its outputs out at its boundary. On every engine the bytes a host reads are identical, and a value read
before a write is intact after it: the read was a copy.
